taxonomyNote: Formerly placed in the monotypic genus Nyctea (still used by Animal Diversity Web); NatureServe places it in Bubo.
fieldMarks: About 61 cm, bulky and round-headed with yellow eyes; wingspan about 1.4 m
White with variable black barring: young females heavily marked, old males almost pure white
behavior: Often hunts by day from a perch, watching for prey, then pursuing it in swift flight
Eats lemmings and voles where available, plus hares, rabbits, ground squirrels and birds
Nomadic; the number moving south each winter varies with prey populations
Usually silent; hoarse croak and shrill whistle on breeding grounds; males hoot to defend territory
habitat: Open tundra; in winter prairies, fields, marshes, beaches, dunes and large airports.
range: Breeds on Arctic tundra from Alaska and northern Canada to Labrador; many winter on the northern Great Plains and Prairies, with irregular southward irruptions.

lookalikes.name: American barn owl
lookalikes.howToTell: Other white owls seen in most of North America are usually barn owls or downy young of other owls.
